findings.title: SOQL Injection via Dynamic Query
findings.explanation: The method concatenates the caller-provided searchKey directly into a dynamic SOQL string without escaping or binding, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SOQL clauses and potentially read or modify data beyond their permissions.
findings.remediation: Replace the dynamic query with a static SOQL statement that uses a bind variable, e.g. `SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE :('%' + String.escapeSingleQuotes(searchKey) + '%') LIMIT 50`, or use `Database.queryWithBinds` with an allow‑list for field names.

findings.title: Field-Level Security Violation
findings.explanation: The method queries and returns the Email and Birthdate fields, which are not readable by users with the Contact Phone Editor permission set. Apex runs in system mode and ignores FLS unless explicitly enforced, so users can view data they should not see.
findings.remediation: Enforce FLS by using WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED in the SOQL query, or by calling Security.stripInaccessible on the queried fields, or by removing the non‑required fields from the query.

findings.title: Record-level sharing bypass in @AuraEnabled method
findings.explanation: The class is declared "without sharing", so record-level sharing rules are ignored. Because the method is exposed via @AuraEnabled, any user with the permission set can invoke it and retrieve cases they should not see, bypassing sharing restrictions.
findings.remediation: Declare the class with "with sharing" or "inherited sharing", or add a WITH SHARE clause to the SOQL query. This ensures that only records the user is allowed to see are returned.

findings.title: Excessive permissions in Support Agent Tools permission set
findings.explanation: The permission set grants ModifyAllData and ViewAllData, which allow users to bypass all sharing and field-level security on every object. This far exceeds the described purpose of only viewing and closing cases.
findings.remediation: Remove the ModifyAllData and ViewAllData permissions from the permission set. Grant only the necessary Case object permissions (Read, Edit) and any other minimal permissions required for the support agent role.

findings.title: FLS not enforced in ContactSearchController
findings.explanation: The SOQL query returns Contact fields without using WITH USER_MODE or Security.stripInaccessible, so field‑level security is ignored and the user can see fields they may not be allowed to view.
findings.remediation: Add WITH USER_MODE to the SOQL query or call Security.stripInaccessible on the result to enforce field‑level security.

findings.title: Without sharing in Aura‑enabled class
findings.explanation: The class is declared without sharing, so record‑level sharing rules are bypassed. A guest user can retrieve all contacts that match the last name, regardless of sharing settings.
findings.remediation: Declare the class with sharing (or inherited sharing) or use WITH USER_MODE to enforce sharing rules.

findings.title: Guest user can access contact data via Aura endpoint
findings.explanation: The Guest User profile has access to ContactSearchController, which exposes contact data to unauthenticated users through the Aura endpoint.
findings.remediation: Remove the class from the guest profile or restrict the method to authenticated users, and enforce sharing and FLS as above.
